questions.question: Using the schedule (R20: D50, S200; R16: D80, S160; R12: D120, S120; R8: D170, S80; R4: D230, S30), identify the equilibrium price and quantity and calculate the surplus or shortage at R16 and at R8.
questions.expected_answer: Equilibrium price R12, equilibrium quantity 120 muffins (demand equals supply). At R16: 160 - 80 = 80 surplus (excess supply). At R8: 170 - 80 = 90 shortage (excess demand).

questions.question: Explain how the market moves back to equilibrium when the price is above equilibrium.
questions.expected_answer: Above equilibrium, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating a surplus; sellers lower the price to sell unsold stock; as price falls, quantity demanded rises (movement down the demand curve) and quantity supplied falls (movement down the supply curve) until they are equal at the equilibrium price.

questions.question: State the effect on equilibrium price and quantity of: (a) an increase in demand; (b) a decrease in supply; (c) an increase in supply.
questions.expected_answer: (a) Price rises, quantity rises (e.g. R12 to R16, 120 to 160). (b) Price rises, quantity falls (e.g. R12 to R16, 120 to 80). (c) Price falls, quantity rises.
